name: Frontline Roster EVERYONE - Weekly Monday 4AM Arizona

parameters.sqlQuery:
-- EVERYONE-level Frontline roster: agents AND managers.
--
-- Source: cs_datawarehouse.vw_dim_employee_detail, employee/day grain keyed on
-- EmID + DateValue. Schema confirmed by probe on 2026-09-11: 27 columns, with
-- EmID, EmployeeName, EmailAddress, samaccountname, TitleName, SkillLevel,
-- Team, SiteName, Country, RegionName, StartDate, WgID, MgrEmID, DateValue.
--
-- Why not the old source: tbl_..._performance_manager has emid NULL across all
-- 128,694 'Day' rows and only 39 of 20,599 active Frontline rows carry any
-- identity, so it can only ever yield managers. It is still used here, but only
-- as a WORKGROUP LOOKUP, which is the one thing it still does well.
--
-- Why not vw_customer_service_master_reporting: the same probe returned 0
-- columns for it - no access.
--
-- Manager name and email come from a SELF-JOIN of the view on MgrEmID = EmID,
-- so they are real employee records rather than the shifted hierarchy columns
-- the old source exposed.

WITH view_latest AS (
  SELECT MAX(DateValue) AS snap
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_datawarehouse.vw_dim_employee_detail`
  WHERE DateValue BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
                      AND CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix')
),
cs_latest AS (
  SELECT MAX(date) AS snap
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager`
  WHERE datetype = 'Day'
    AND date BETWEEN DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 30 DAY)
                 AND CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix')
),
-- Workgroup names + the 3-level hierarchy, one row per WgID.
-- The view carries only WgID, no workgroup name, so this supplies both the
-- names and the 12056 ancestry test.
wg AS (
  SELECT
    SAFE_CAST(t.wgid AS INT64) AS wgid,
    ANY_VALUE(TRIM(CAST(t.workgroup AS STRING)))       AS workgroup,
    ANY_VALUE(TRIM(CAST(t.parentworkgroup AS STRING))) AS parentworkgroup,
    -- >>>>>>>>>>>>>> FRONTLINE SCOPE - WORKGROUP 12056 <<<<<<<<<<<<<<
    -- DEPTH LIMIT: the lookup table denormalizes only three levels, so 12056
    -- matches only when it sits at most two levels above the workgroup. Deeper
    -- branches (e.g. 12056 -> B2B and Canada -> Multiple Contacts -> MC Team 1)
    -- are NOT matched. If the count looks short, that is why.
    -- ALTERNATIVE, no depth limit: delete the  WHERE w.in_scope = 1  line at the
    -- bottom and instead filter the final SELECT on the view's own Team column,
    -- e.g.  WHERE p.Team = 'Frontline'
    MAX(IF(12056 IN (
      SAFE_CAST(t.wgid AS INT64),
      SAFE_CAST(t.parentwgid AS INT64),
      SAFE_CAST(t.grandparentwgid AS INT64)
    ), 1, 0)) AS in_scope
    -- >>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>>> END SCOPE <<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<<
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` AS t
  CROSS JOIN cs_latest AS cl
  WHERE t.datetype = 'Day'
    AND t.date = cl.snap
  GROUP BY wgid
),
-- One row per employee on the newest snapshot. No explicit active flag exists
-- on this view, so presence in the latest snapshot is what "current" means.
people AS (
  SELECT v.*
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_datawarehouse.vw_dim_employee_detail` AS v
  CROSS JOIN view_latest AS vl
  WHERE v.DateValue = vl.snap
  QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
    PARTITION BY v.EmID ORDER BY v.DateValue DESC, v.created_datetime DESC
  ) = 1
)
SELECT
  COALESCE(CAST(p.EmID AS STRING), '')                        AS `Employee ID`,
  -- "First Last". Source may store "Last, First"; the regex swaps the halves
  -- and passes a comma-less name through unchanged.
  COALESCE(TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(CAST(p.EmployeeName AS STRING)), r'^([^,]+),\s*(.+)$', r'\2 \1')), '')                              AS `Full Name`,
  COALESCE(LOWER(TRIM(CAST(p.EmailAddress AS STRING))), '')   AS `Email Address`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(p.samaccountname AS STRING)), '')        AS `Sam Account Name`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(p.TitleName AS STRING)), '')             AS `Job Title`,
  COALESCE(CAST(p.SkillLevel AS STRING), '')                  AS `Skill Level`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(p.Team AS STRING)), '')                  AS `Team`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(p.SiteName AS STRING)), '')              AS `Office Location`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(p.Country AS STRING)), '')               AS `Country`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(CAST(p.RegionName AS STRING)), '')            AS `Region`,
  IFNULL(FORMAT_DATE('%m/%d/%Y', SAFE_CAST(p.StartDate AS DATE)), '') AS `Start Date`,
  COALESCE(CAST(p.WgID AS STRING), '')                        AS `Work Group ID`,
  COALESCE(w.workgroup, '')                                   AS `Work Group`,
  COALESCE(w.parentworkgroup, '')                             AS `Parent Work Group`,
  COALESCE(CAST(p.MgrEmID AS STRING), '')                     AS `Manager's Employee ID`,
  COALESCE(TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(CAST(m.EmployeeName AS STRING)), r'^([^,]+),\s*(.+)$', r'\2 \1')), '')                              AS `Manager's Name`,
  COALESCE(LOWER(TRIM(CAST(m.EmailAddress AS STRING))), '')   AS `Manager's Email`,
  COALESCE(CAST(p.DateValue AS STRING), '')                   AS `Snapshot Date`
FROM people AS p
LEFT JOIN wg     AS w ON w.wgid = p.WgID
LEFT JOIN people AS m ON m.EmID = p.MgrEmID
WHERE w.in_scope = 1
ORDER BY `Manager's Name`, `Full Name`

-- Runs ONLY when the roster returns zero rows. Reports each stage separately
-- so the losing stage is named rather than guessed.
WITH view_latest AS (
  SELECT MAX(DateValue) AS snap
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_datawarehouse.vw_dim_employee_detail`
  WHERE DateValue >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 60 DAY)
),
cs_latest AS (
  SELECT MAX(date) AS snap
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager`
  WHERE datetype = 'Day'
    AND date >= DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE('America/Phoenix'), INTERVAL 60 DAY)
),
view_stats AS (
  SELECT
    CAST((SELECT snap FROM view_latest) AS STRING) AS view_latest_date,
    COUNT(*)                    AS view_rows,
    COUNT(DISTINCT v.EmID)      AS view_employees,
    COUNT(DISTINCT v.WgID)      AS view_workgroups,
    COUNT(v.EmployeeName)       AS name_nonnull,
    COUNT(v.EmailAddress)       AS email_nonnull,
    COUNT(v.MgrEmID)            AS mgremid_nonnull
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_datawarehouse.vw_dim_employee_detail` AS v
  WHERE v.DateValue = (SELECT snap FROM view_latest)
),
wg_scope AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT SAFE_CAST(t.wgid AS INT64) AS wgid
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_reporting.tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager` AS t
  WHERE t.datetype = 'Day'
    AND t.date = (SELECT snap FROM cs_latest)
    AND 12056 IN (
      SAFE_CAST(t.wgid AS INT64),
      SAFE_CAST(t.parentwgid AS INT64),
      SAFE_CAST(t.grandparentwgid AS INT64)
    )
),
scope_stats AS (
  SELECT
    CAST((SELECT snap FROM cs_latest) AS STRING) AS cs_latest_date,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM wg_scope)              AS workgroups_in_scope
),
overlap AS (
  SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT v.EmID) AS employees_in_scope
  FROM `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_datawarehouse.vw_dim_employee_detail` AS v
  WHERE v.DateValue = (SELECT snap FROM view_latest)
    AND v.WgID IN (SELECT wgid FROM wg_scope)
)
SELECT * FROM view_stats CROSS JOIN scope_stats CROSS JOIN overlap

parameters.content:
## Frontline Roster - EVERYONE - Weekly Monday 4AM Arizona

### This is agents AND managers
Source switched to `wf-gcp-us-ae-cs-prod.cs_datawarehouse.vw_dim_employee_detail`, employee/day grain keyed on EmID + DateValue. Schema confirmed by probe on 2026-09-11: 27 columns.

The old source, tbl_customer_service_employee_performance_manager, could only ever yield managers - emid is NULL across all 128,694 'Day' rows and only 39 of 20,599 active Frontline rows carried any identity. It is still used here, but ONLY as a workgroup-name and hierarchy lookup, which is what it still does well.

vw_customer_service_master_reporting returned 0 columns on the probe - no access - so it is not used.

### Manager data is now real
Manager's Name and Manager's Email come from a SELF-JOIN of the view on MgrEmID = EmID. These are genuine employee records, not the shifted hierarchy columns the old source exposed, so the level confusion is gone.

### Job Title is back
TitleName exists on this view, so Job Title returns after being removed as unsourceable. Skill Level, Country and Region are new too.

### 18 columns
Employee ID, Full Name, Email Address, Sam Account Name, Job Title, Skill Level, Team, Office Location, Country, Region, Start Date, Work Group ID, Work Group, Parent Work Group, Manager's Employee ID, Manager's Name, Manager's Email, Snapshot Date.

Full Name and Manager's Name render "First Last". The regex swaps "Last, First" and passes a comma-less name through unchanged, so it is correct either way.

This workflow REPLACES row 1 of the tab.

### Scope: workgroup 12056 - depth limit applies
The view has no workgroup name and no ancestry, only WgID. The 12056 test therefore runs against the lookup table's three levels (wgid, parentwgid, grandparentwgid), so 12056 matches only when it sits at most two levels above a workgroup. Deeper branches such as
  12056 -> B2B and Canada -> Multiple Contacts -> MC Team 1
are NOT matched. Multiple Contacts teams may be absent.

NO-DEPTH-LIMIT ALTERNATIVE: the view carries its own Team column. Replace
  WHERE w.in_scope = 1
with
  WHERE p.Team = 'Frontline'
Team is an output column so you can see the real values first.

### There is no active flag
This view has no active or termination column. Presence in the latest DateValue snapshot is what "current" means here.

### Safety
Zero rows means the sheet is NOT cleared and the run fails with a stage-by-stage profile: rows on the latest snapshot, workgroups resolved in scope, and employees overlapping that scope. It names which stage lost the rows and gives the one-line fix.

30-day snapshot window on both sources, deliberately narrow so stale data is never published as current.

### Schedule
Workflow timezone America/Phoenix, cron 0 4 * * 1 = 11:00 UTC year-round, Arizona has no DST. Confirm the timezone in Workflow Settings after import.

### After import
Select credentials on the two BigQuery nodes and the two Sheets nodes, run manually, check the summary for employee_row_count and teams_present, then activate.
